claims.text: The baseline FeMnNiGeSi films on SiO2 have substrate-induced strain.
The baseline FeMnNiGeSi films on SiO2 have limited thermal dissipation.
Diamond or SiC can provide a high-thermal-conductivity, low-lattice-mismatch substrate for the specified FeMnNiGeSi films.
Appropriate buffer layers can decouple or control substrate-induced strain in the FeMnNiGeSi films.
Changing the substrate or buffer layer changes interfacial strain in the FeMnNiGeSi film.
Changing the substrate or buffer layer changes thermal boundary resistance at the FeMnNiGeSi film interface.
Interfacial strain and thermal boundary resistance modify microstructural ordering in the FeMnNiGeSi film.
Interfacial strain and thermal boundary resistance modify local magnetic exchange interactions in the FeMnNiGeSi film.
Lower or less disruptive substrate-induced strain alleviates magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Lower or less disruptive substrate-induced strain reduces heterogeneity in magnetic exchange.
Higher substrate thermal conductivity enables more efficient heat transfer during rapid magnetic-cooling cycles.
Alleviating domain-wall pinning and exchange heterogeneity produces a sharper and more reproducible magnetocaloric response.
Alleviating domain-wall pinning and exchange heterogeneity reduces magnetic hysteresis.
High-conductivity, low-mismatch substrates or suitable buffer layers will produce a more pronounced magnetocaloric entropy change than the SiO2 baseline under low-field cycling.
High-conductivity, low-mismatch substrates or suitable buffer layers will produce a narrower magnetic hysteresis loop than the SiO2 baseline under low-field cycling.
The SiO2-supported baseline displays relatively high hysteresis.
The SiO2-supported baseline displays a broadened magnetocaloric transition.
Substrate properties are well established to influence strain and heat transfer.
